Everything below is read off the tree at the head, not off the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set, console reading of a BARE string in a predicate slot (nav `visible`, node `visibleWhen` / `visible` / `hidden` / `disabled`, action `visible` / `disabled` / `condition`, row predicates, settings `visible`, toolbar-action `visible`):

- Newly ACCEPTED (evaluated instead of faulting): every CEL-only construct — `in` over a list, `size()`, `has()`, `.contains()`, `today()`, CEL `.?` selection, the spec's own example `'org_owner' in current_user.positions`, the card's `size(page.items) > 0`. Each of these was always accepted by the spec and the server: `ExpressionInputSchema` / `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` transform the string arm to `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` (packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts L190-193, L269-273) and `normalizeExpression` parses that envelope and compiles it on `ExpressionEngine` (packages/formula/src/normalize.ts L33-62). RIGHT — the console joins the contract it already declared.
- Newly FAULTED (were evaluated on the JS grammar): `===`, `!==`, `?.`, `??`, ternary `a ? b : c`, `typeof`, JS methods (`.includes(`, `.length`, `.filter(`, `.map(`, `.toUpperCase(` …), single-param arrows, and a read of a key the bound map does not hold (`data.status` on a `data: {}` host read `undefined` and compared clean; CEL answers `No such key: status`). None of these was ever accepted by the spec or the server: the string arm is CEL by definition and the CEL compiler refuses them at `objectstack compile` / publish. RIGHT, and correctly declared as a narrowing of what the CONSOLE tolerated, not of the protocol. Measured on the head: a repo-wide grep for a predicate key followed by a string carrying `===` / `!==` / `.includes(` / `.length` / `?.` outside tests hits 2 lines, both in `skills/objectui` (the lines follow-up #27587 names); the dev's "0 authored non-test predicates" holds.
- The missing-key consequence per slot, pinned by the flipped tests: a show-key node gate stays hidden (same verdict, now a fault line instead of the adapter-only dev line); a bare `hidden` gate goes from shown to concealed; a bare `disabled` gate goes from enabled to disabled; the fail-soft `useCondition` leg goes from `false` to `true`; the nav gate withholds. Each is the slot's pre-existing fault direction (objectui#13299, #11212, #12700), applied to a predicate that the server would also fault on. RIGHT.
- Public surface of `@object-ui/core` (re-exported by `@object-ui/react`): `toPredicateInput(string)` now returns `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` instead of `'${string}'`; the `EvaluatorPredicateInput` type is unchanged and both members were already in it; a `${…}` string is still returned as-is; a non-`cel` envelope's `source` is still wrapped. Idempotence holds by value (the parity test moved from `toBe` to `toEqual`, honestly: the envelope branch re-emits a fresh equal object). RIGHT, and named in the changeset.
- `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateCondition`: branch order on the head is unevaluable → `cel` envelope → unwrap other envelope (remembered) → blank → absent → `${` template → bare string to `evaluateCelCondition` → legacy only for the unwrapped non-`cel` `source`. A bare string therefore reaches the same `evalFieldPredicate` seam as the envelope with the same `onFault` / `throwOnError` contract, and the same bag (`record` pinned when present, the whole bag as `extra`, `current_user` permissions and capabilities ridden on the subject). RIGHT. The blank bare string `'   '` now arrives as the blank `cel` envelope and is answered by `answerBlankGate` (diagnosed "no gate", ADR-0137 D4) — one report, one dedupe key for both spellings. RIGHT.
- `evalRowPredicate`: a bare non-template string goes to the CEL path; `isLegacyDialectSource` still fires its one-time prescription line for any legacy marker, so a bare `===` row predicate prints the prescription AND the engine's fault line, once each — two lines, both true, the first carrying the rewrite. Acceptable.
- `evaluatePlainCondition` (exported from `@object-ui/core`, no console caller, its own tests pin `===`) still reads a bare string on the JS grammar. Not in the claim surface; declared out of scope in the PR. See ③.
- Comment-only edits in `ExpressionProvider.tsx` and `SchemaRenderer.tsx`: each describes the route the code now takes; the `isCelEnvelope` hoist guard's rationale is correctly restated (stripping the envelope no longer changes engines). RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27457-bare-string-predicate-cel.md`: `'@object-ui/core': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a BREAKING banner, exactly one `adr-0087` marker. PR body carries the same two declaration lines plus `Skills-docs: follow-up #27587`. Lines match on both carriers.
- Level: `narrowed` is a kind other than `none` on a package the diff moves ⇒ at least `minor` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). `minor` is the right level. Only `@object-ui/core` is bumped; the other touched packages ship comments and tests only, and dependents take the internal-dependency bump. Right.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: judged against step 3 — a FROM-TO mapping is owed when the diff removes or renames something an author can write under the protocol (a spec key, an export, a config field). Nothing protocol-legal moves: the spellings that now fault were refused by the spec's string arm and by the server's compile step before this PR, so no stored row the server accepted changes meaning and `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. The gate's own honesty check for this category (body must carry no prescription — `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` L147-153, arrow / `## Migration` / FROM-TO label detectors) is satisfied: the body has no arrow and no migration heading. HOLDS. The teaching of the CEL spellings is correctly routed to the skills follow-up rather than into the CHANGELOG.
- One prose defect (should-fix, below): the changeset's last BREAKING sentence tells an upgrader that a predicate "that must keep the legacy reading can be spelled as a `${…}` template". That is a console-only spelling the spec does not model as a predicate and the server will not read; shipping it in CHANGELOG.md advertises a second dialect the triage direction ("no legacy path") set out to remove, and the PR body's "The changeset carries a rewrite guide" misdescribes a body that, correctly for its disposition, carries none.
- Check-runs on the head at read time: 52 total — 13 success, 11 skipped, 28 in_progress. Success includes Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core, Type Check · source gates / workspace / debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate (its 3 shards path-skipped), Live E2E UI, Build UI Deps. In progress: all 16 `Test UI` shards, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, and the 8 root `Lint ·` lanes (the one that runs `check-adr-0087-registration` among them). Their conclusions are the gate verdicts for the pin sweep, the ui type-check and the ADR-0087 marker; this record does not pre-empt them — the queue waits for green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6498493316 is on head `223d913f`; the head of record adds `14d03c24` (changeset: the narrowing arm, BREAKING banner, disposition) and `827769ad` (three more pin flips: `page-header-predicate-dialect`, `record-alert.loadingFrameDiagnostic`, `useCondition.canonSpelling`). Both are judged from the diff above; the three flips are substantive (verdict + paired CEL control + reason text), not weakened.

- Deviation 1 — in-place fix of `listConditional.ts` outside the claim surface: ANSWERED. The superseding claim 6498534084 adds the file to the surface; same defect class, ablation leg 3 red without it.
- Deviation 2 — full ui vitest sweep stopped at 86 min, 8 failing files all flipped: ANSWERED BY THE GATE. The 16 `Test UI` shards on the head are the measurement; in progress at read time.
- Deviation 3 — dogfood battery "n/a: no `!` in the title and no (narrowing) arm": STALE ON THE HEAD. The arm was added at `14d03c24`, after the report; `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` L274 owes the full battery once on the final head whenever the Clause line carries `(narrowing)`, and CI's Dogfood shards are path-skipped on this head. Grade: should-fix, not FAIL — `packages/qa/dogfood` has zero `@object-ui` / `ExpressionEvaluator` references, so this diff cannot move it; the seat either runs it once on `827769ad` and records `dogfood_battery`, or records that reading as the exemption.
- `open_questions`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: `evaluatePlainCondition` legacy reading, carrier "none". Should-fix: it is a published export whose bare-string reading contradicts the spec (a residual second grammar on the public surface); PD #10 wants a carrier for a contract violation — file a card, do not expand this diff.
- Skills deferral (`Skills-docs: follow-up #27587`): ACCEPTABLE, with a condition. `skills/**` is Tier H (PD #14), so it could not land inside a default-tier card thread; the spelling `follow-up #N` is the claim template's; #27587 is open, names the exact lines (`schema-expressions.md` L10, L83-89, L254, L335-336; `protocol.md` L17) and carries the FROM-TO teaching the changeset rightly does not. Until it lands, `skills/objectui` teaches `===`, `?.`, `??`, `.includes()` as condition syntax that the console now faults on — the card's own "should land with or right after #27584" is the condition the seat holds.
- Seat premise re-measured on the head: `evaluateCondition` routes a bare string to CEL at L434-436; the legacy branch at L441 is reachable only with `unwrappedEnvelope === true`. The dispatch's acceptance (nav `visible` and page `visibleWhen` as bare CEL evaluate on CEL; restoring the legacy route turns the tests red) is pinned by the two new acceptance files, each with a polarity pair, an envelope control and a legacy-only `===` counter-case.

### ④ Design judgment

Held against the code it cites and the accepted scenario; tried to break on fault policy, missing roots, list paths and double evaluation.

- `ExpressionEvaluator.ts` — HOLDS. The funnel claim is true on the tree: every console predicate reader reaches `evaluateCondition` (SchemaRenderer L1455/L1476/L1592, ExpressionProvider L598/L669/L682, ActionEngine L287, ActionRunner L1544/L1577, useCondition L222/L241, containers.tsx L762/L842, SettingsView L45, managedByEmptyState L84, listConditional L321), and several hand it the raw authored value, so resolving the shorthand here is the console's equivalent of the server's input step. Roots: the nav bag (`buildExpressionScope`) binds `current_user` / `user` / `features`; the node bag (`buildNodeEvaluationScope`) binds `record`, `current_user`, `page.VAR`; SettingsView binds `data` — the scenario's `current_user.positions` and `page.items` resolve, and the tests prove it with opposite verdicts on the two polarities. Fault policy per slot is untouched: `onFault` single call on the fail-soft legs, the `throwOnError` two-call probe only where it already ran for envelopes (ActionEngine, DeclaredActionsBar, dev-mode node gate, nav second ask on fault). No new double evaluation: a bare string now pays exactly what its envelope paid. The `throwOnError` message split (generic `CEL predicate failed to evaluate: SOURCE` vs `onFault`'s `[kind] message`) pre-dates this PR and is pinned as such. Non-`cel` envelopes: `template` envelopes are produced only for text slots (`actionCopyTemplate`, `record-title`, `titleFormat`), so the kept legacy route for an unwrapped non-`cel` `source` is dormant and harmless.
- `predicateInput.ts` — HOLDS. The string branch emits the spec's own normalized value; `wrapIfBare` survives only for the non-`cel` envelope branch; `hasDeclaredPredicate` (derived from this normalizer) keeps its three states — the blank bare string is now the blank `cel` envelope the evaluator diagnoses, which the `declaredPredicate` and `ActionRunner.disabledGate` tests re-pin.
- `listConditional.ts` — HOLDS. `source.includes('${')` is the only legacy router; the row is still pinned as `record` after the host spread on both paths; `warnLegacyDialect` keeps firing for any marker so the prescription channel survives the route change; the fail-closed route reports `[parse]` for a bare `===` and `[legacy]` only for a template (pinned).
- `ExpressionProvider.tsx`, `SchemaRenderer.tsx` — comment-only; each matches the route the code now takes. The nav gate's "fault ⇒ withheld" and the node gate's "fault ⇒ withheld" are what turned the original bug into "hidden for everyone"; with the bare string on CEL those same policies now withhold only a predicate the server would also refuse.
- Pin sweep — HOLDS. Every flipped pin asserts the new semantics' substance: the CEL verdict on a matching row, the paired `==` / `.contains()` control, the report count, and the reason text (`No such key: status`, `Unknown variable: bogus_unbound_field`, `Reason: [parse]`, `CEL predicate failed to evaluate: …`); legs whose subject was the adapter-only `data.*` diagnostic keep it through the `${…}` spelling, the one that still evaluates cleanly against the wrong object, and gain a sibling case pinning where the bare spelling went. No pin was deleted or weakened to "old assertion gone". The two fixture `===` in `record-block-record-reach` are rewritten to `==`, which is the fix the card asks of authored metadata.

Findings (none must-fix):

- should-fix — changeset BREAKING paragraph: drop or reword "can be spelled as a `${…}` template"; point the upgrader at the CEL spelling (`==`, `in`, `.contains()`, `size()`, `has()`) without a FROM-TO list, so the disposition stays honest and the CHANGELOG stops advertising a console-only dialect. Fix the PR body's "carries a rewrite guide" in the same stroke.
- should-fix — run the dogfood battery once on the final head (or record the zero-coupling reading as the exemption) and refresh the report's `head` / `dogfood_battery` fields.
- should-fix — file a card for `evaluatePlainCondition`'s legacy bare-string reading (published export, no console caller) instead of carrier "none".
- condition — land #27587 with or right after this PR; until then the skill and the runtime disagree on the operator table.
